scope: Proposition 7.1 (Distribution through a dyadic hierarchy) of the manuscript “Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states” (preprints/Polynomial-PEPS-approximation-of-gapped-square-grid-ground-states-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 265 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0b55ba0b87ad0468), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For all sufficiently large L, there is a protocol with the following properties. All constants in this statement are uniform in the Hamiltonian and L. 1. There are O(L2) parties, one for each square in a padded dyadic hierarchy and at most a fixed number of additional parties for each repainting of a square. Initialization is a pure product across parties. One party initially holds the main copy of Ω; all auxiliary copies are initialized privately at their designated parties. 2. The schedule has at most CL3 changes. Each change is implemented by a fixed number of contraction gates involving at most a fixed number of parties and having the bipartite-resource expansions established in Lemmas 6.3, 6.5, and 6.6. The expansions can be made accurate to any fixed inverse power of L in operator norm where an approximation is needed. Each party participates in at most a fixed number of gates involving other parties over its entire lifetime. 3. Every linked gate involves parties at the same or adjacent dyadic scales. Parties at a gate have addresses at distance O(n) from one another, where n is either endpoint scale; additional parties have the scale and address of the square to whose repainting they belong. 4. There is a designated reference vector at every stage, formed from the main encoded frame and the auxiliary encoded frames. All its factors have norm at most one. Each change takes its preceding reference vector within CL−20 in vector norm of its following reference vector. At the end, the reference is Ω ⊗ Ξ, 1 − CL3−60 ≤ ∥Ξ∥ ≤ 1, where Ξ contains only registers to be discarded. Every original physical site is a raw register at its own unit-square party. No other party has a physical output, so every party’s physical output dimension is at most q.
